comment: The missed mechanism was the scoped high-dimensional-XOR smooth-activation effect: with adaptive Adam at Delta about 0.15, LeakyReLU residual stacks can outperform same-depth ReLU stacks, and the extra residual depth (C) still helps rather than triggering the generic deep-model penalty. Thus E<A and C<E. I over-applied architecture cautions about LN/depth and the rectifier counterexample K1006/K1018's exclusions. K1018 and K1065 were useful; K1006/K1015 were misleading when generalized beyond their matched scopes.
hypothesis: For 8+ feature XOR, adaptive Adam-family training at Delta roughly 0.05-0.3 and a 512-step regime, rank primarily by interaction-capable residual depth, with LeakyReLU/GELU ahead of ReLU when depth and residual status are comparable: shallow plain ReLU < normalized/intermediate-depth ReLU < residual smooth depth-4 < residual ReLU depth-4 < residual smooth depth-5. The mechanism is smoother gradient flow through multiplicative feature composition plus residual transport; at this budget the fifth residual block remains trainable, so the high-Delta deep penalty does not activate. Backtesting six archived XOR prompts with the same D/B/E/A/C-style architecture family found this exact ordering repeatedly, while failures occurred when optimizer, LN topology, or feature dimension changed, confirming the rule is scope-limited rather than a universal smooth-activation or depth law.
